clue.text: Celebrate tum and pert bust

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters of the words before it are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is cheering a tummy and a perky bosom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' looks like part of the body in the surface but signals the anagram: TUM and PERT rearrange to make the answer; 'and' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To trumpet something is to proclaim or celebrate it loudly, a verb sense from the instrument.

clue.text: First woman to be caught by this group of criminals?

indicators.note: to be caught by means held inside, so the woman's name goes within the next word

parts.note: taken as written
Eve is the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: A question: will the first woman be nabbed by this criminal gang?
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' does double work in the surface, sounding like a pointer to the gang, but it also supplies letters; the woman's name sits after its I.
explanation.definitionFit: Thieves are those who steal, and together they can form a criminal gang.

clue.text: University growth — it's mythical

parts.note: a corn is a hard growth of skin on the foot

explanation.surface: A university growth is said to be a myth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growth' is not expansion but the skin growth on a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: The unicorn is a one-horned horse of legend, a creature of myth.

clue.text: Silver dish

definitions.meaning: silverware or gilt tableware is collectively called by this name
a flat dish from which food is eaten

explanation.definitionFit: Plate means both precious-metal tableware and a flat dish for food.

clue.text: Behaviour shown by mate swimming in river

indicators.note: in means the anagram sits inside the name of the river

parts.note: the Trent is a major river in the English Midlands

indicators.note: swimming suggests moving about, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

explanation.surface: A friend's behaviour while swimming in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' turns the friend into ATME. The Trent is a river in central England. 'shown by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatment is the way one behaves towards someone, their conduct or handling of them.

clue.text: Worker almost loaded — one's difficult to control

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: loaded means full

explanation.surface: A labourer has nearly a full load and is hard to manage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the last letter from FULL to leave FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: A handful is idiomatic for a person, often a child, who is hard to manage.

clue.text: Lucky chap — pyjamas fitted

indicators.note: fitted means the answer is fitted inside the words before it

explanation.surface: A fortunate man has pyjamas that fit.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'cHAP PYjamas'.
explanation.definitionFit: Happy can mean fortunate or lucky, as in a happy coincidence.

clue.text: It's within your grasp unless you're online

definitions.text: It's within your grasp unless you're online

parts.words: It's within your grasp unless you're online
parts.note: sounds like something attainable, but literally means a thing held in the hands, the printed version of what many now read on screen

explanation.surface: Something is achievable unless you are connected to the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within your grasp' means physically held: you hold the printed daily in your hands unless you read the news online.
explanation.definitionFit: A printed daily is held in the hands, unlike its online edition.

clue.text: Recipe's milk substitute

definitions.meaning: a recipe in the sense of a set method or prescription; 's means is, joining the two senses
the powdered preparation fed to babies in place of breast milk

explanation.definitionFit: A formula is a set method or recipe, and also the infant milk preparation.

clue.text: First to land on snakes? Just the opposite

definitions.text: First to land on snakes? Just the opposite

parts.words: First to land on snakes? Just the opposite
parts.note: in the board game of snakes and the other things, landing on a snake sends you down; the opposite is what carries you up, and they come second in the name

explanation.surface: Someone advises landing on snakes first, then says the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: In the board game Snakes and ———, snakes take you down and the other pieces take you up.
explanation.definitionFit: In the board game, these are what lift a player upward, the opposite of snakes.

clue.text: Parrot's wild — I tame it

definitions.note: the definition is Parrot with 's standing for is, linking to the wordplay

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters of the following words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A pet bird is untamed, so its owner vows to train it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parrot' looks like the bird but is the verb, to repeat or copy; 's is short for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat or copy another's words mechanically, just as a mimic does.

clue.text: Charged wartime inmate with initially erroneous links to Communist

parts.note: POW is a prisoner of war, an inmate of a wartime camp

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: red is a familiar label for a communist

explanation.surface: A prisoner of war is accused of mistaken ties to the communists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'links to' only joins the pieces; 'Charged' means energised, not accused.
explanation.definitionFit: Powered and charged both describe something supplied with electrical energy.

clue.text: Cruelly, lovely tin gets smashed

indicators.note: smashed means broken to pieces, so the letters of the preceding words are reassembled

explanation.surface: A pretty tin is cruelly smashed.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting violently means acting with brutal force, which is close to acting cruelly.

clue.text: Break hands, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is judged by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: paws is a jocular word for hands

explanation.surface: Someone breaks their hands, according to rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break' looks like a verb, but it is the noun meaning a rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause is a short break or rest in activity.

clue.text: Cavity walls in usual houses

indicators.note: houses means contains, so the answer is held within the run of words before it

explanation.surface: Cavity walls are typical in ordinary houses.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about building insulation; the answer sits across 'walls in usual'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinus is a hollow cavity in the bones of the skull.

clue.text: Talk about winter in Paris and what you might be doing

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for talk goes round the French word

parts.note: to sing is slang for to talk to the police, to inform
hiver is French for winter

explanation.surface: Chatting about winter in Paris and what you would be up to there.
explanation.walkthrough: To sing is underworld slang for informing; hiver is French. In winter you might well be trembling with cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Trembling from cold is what you might be doing in a winter, as the clue's scene suggests.

clue.text: Swedes perhaps cultivated from one pasture when temperature drops

indicators.note: cultivated means worked like soil, so the letters are turned over and rearranged
drops means falls away, so the letter for temperature is removed from the fodder

explanation.surface: Swede vegetables are grown on a field once the weather turns colder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swedes' looks like the root vegetable, fitting 'cultivated' and 'pasture', but means people from Sweden. ONE PASTURE loses T, and the remaining letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Swedes are one example of people from the continent of Europe, as the 'perhaps' signals.

clue.text: Right schooling? Not a drop

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter A is taken away from the word for schooling

parts.note: education means schooling

explanation.surface: Is the right sort of schooling teetotal?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a drop' reads like abstinence, but 'Not a' removes an A and 'drop' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A reduction is a decrease or fall, which is to say a drop.

clue.text: Flown to hospital and manner improved

parts.note: an air is a manner or bearing
lifted means raised or improved

explanation.surface: A patient was taken to hospital and their demeanour brightened.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone airlifted is carried by aircraft, as when an injured person is flown to hospital.

clue.text: Review of recital — you might read it in The Telegraph

definitions.text: you might read it in The Telegraph

indicators.note: review means look again, so the letters of the word are reconsidered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper critic's write-up of a concert recital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Review' suggests a critic's piece, but signals that RECITAL's letters are reordered.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of writing in a newspaper such as The Telegraph is an article.

clue.text: Set to rights through relaxation or drug?

parts.note: rest means relaxation
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Will rest or medication put someone right?
explanation.walkthrough: 'drug' is not medicine but E, slang for ecstasy. 'through' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore is to bring back to a proper condition, to set things right again.

clue.text: Thatcher's efforts can be seen here

definitions.text: Thatcher's efforts can be seen here

parts.words: Thatcher's efforts can be seen here
parts.note: suggests a political legacy of the former prime minister, but a thatcher is a craftsman who covers the tops of houses with straw

explanation.surface: Margaret Thatcher's achievements are on display here.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Thatcher was a British prime minister; a thatcher lays straw or reed on houses.
explanation.definitionFit: A thatcher's work is laid on the tops of buildings, so the result is visible there.

clue.text: What batsman might be given near end

parts.note: in cricket a batsman is given out by the umpire when dismissed
to come is to draw near or approach

explanation.surface: A batsman might be given out near the close of play.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the umpire gives a batsman out, ending their innings.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome is the end result of something.

clue.text: Head of Government enters Surrey for a change — when he's available for consultation?

indicators.note: enters means goes into, so the letter goes inside the rearranged county
for a change means altered, so the letters of the county are rearranged
head of means the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: The leader of the government visits Surrey for once, to hold consultations.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county south of London; 'for a change' rearranges it, and G goes in. In Britain a doctor's or MP's surgery is the session when they see the public.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a surgery is the set time when a doctor or MP sees people for advice.

clue.text: Exhibiting Degas finally in gallery shows artistic discernment

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the letter goes into the gallery's name

parts.note: the Tate is a famous London art gallery

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A Degas exhibition at the gallery shows good artistic judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of British art galleries in London and elsewhere. 'Exhibiting' and 'shows' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste is the ability to judge what is beautiful or appropriate, especially in art.

clue.text: Meet European by new bar

parts.note: a counter is the bar in a shop or pub

explanation.surface: A European meets a newcomer by the pub bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is only a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An encounter is a meeting, often an unexpected one; both serve as noun or verb.

clue.text: Gradually moved skirt downwards at first

parts.note: to skirt is to go round the edge of

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A hem was lowered bit by bit, starting at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirt' is not the garment but the verb, to border or go round.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge is to move gradually or carefully, little by little.

clue.text: Heading off for a meal — this could be stimulating

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed from the word that follows

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: Someone heads off for a meal that might perk them up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An upper is slang for a stimulant drug, something that gives a lift.

clue.text: Conservative arguing and boasting

parts.note: rowing (rhyming with cowing) means quarrelling

explanation.surface: A Tory politician is quarrelling and bragging.
explanation.walkthrough: Row, rhyming with 'cow', is British for a noisy quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Crowing means boasting or gloating triumphantly, as a cockerel's call suggests.

clue.text: To make progress I recommend embracing proportional representation

indicators.note: embracing means hugging, so the abbreviation goes inside the word for recommend

parts.note: to move is to propose or recommend formally, as at a meeting

explanation.surface: A speaker proposes a fairer voting system as the way forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' is a link; MOVE is the meeting sense, to propose a motion.
explanation.definitionFit: To improve is to get better, which means to make progress.

clue.text: Appeared united after end of debate

indicators.note: after places the word for united behind the letter from debate
end of means the final letter of the word is taken

parts.note: merged means combined or united

explanation.surface: After a debate ended, a united front appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Emerged means came into view, which is to say appeared.

clue.text: A good place to put your blooming little 'uns

definitions.text: A good place to put your blooming little 'uns

parts.words: A good place to put your blooming little 'uns
parts.note: reads like an exasperated parent putting their blasted children somewhere, but blooming also means flowering, so the little ones are young plants

explanation.surface: An exasperated parent suggests where to park the dratted kids.
explanation.walkthrough: Blooming is a mild British oath, like 'bloody'; it also means in flower. The word names both a room for children and a place raising young plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery is both a room for young children and a place where young plants are grown.
